title: Authoring and support
Authoring and support
Authoring and support
text:
Choose a teaching policy
The shared math-exercise defaults offer four steps, ending with a worked solution. Loading policy definitions does not select them. The example site loads feedback/course.yml and explicitly selects its course policy in _quarto.yml:
ai-feedback:
  policy-files: feedback/course.yml
  project-policy:
    math-exercise: course-mathematics
A policy can inherit those defaults and specialize them by name:
# feedback/course.yml
ai-feedback:
  policies:
    course-mathematics:
      max-words: 120
      reset-on-run: true
    brief-mathematics:
      extends: course-mathematics
      max-words: 90
    two-step-practice:
      extends: brief-mathematics
      steps:
        - step-prompt: Ask one guiding question without giving a formula or answer.
        - step-prompt: Give a concise worked explanation of this task.
          allow-full-solution: true
Select the specialization with #| feedback-policy: two-step-practice on a feedback-enabled STACK block. #| label: rational-practice gives it a stable key for YAML exercises.math-exercise overrides. examples.qmd also selects page-policy: {math-exercise: brief-mathematics} in its front matter. Its other cards inherit four steps; only the selected card replaces the sequence with two. Omitted fields inherit, while a supplied steps list replaces every step and its permissions. base-prompt changes the continuing teaching instructions; step-prompt describes one step. Use neither the retired prompt field nor an authored integrations/defaults section.
Edits clear stale feedback and Check evidence while preserving hint progress. Check resets progress by default; a selected policy can set reset-on-run: false to preserve it. Selecting a different variant always restarts progress. Feedback collects a snapshot without running validation, grading, or authored tests.

title: Authoring and support
text:
What the adapter checks







Supported here
Scope




Source
Moodle STACK XML <quiz> with named STACK questions; category and description entries are skipped.


Inputs
Scalar algebraic and numerical text answers, with strict syntax and <insertstars>0</insertstars> or <insertstars>1</insertstars>. Mode 0 requires *; mode 1 also accepts adjacent 2x, 2(x+1), (x+1)(x-1), and (x+1)x. Both keep xy as one symbol; whitespace alone never means multiplication. Other insertstars modes fail at import.


Variables
A small, safely parsed Maxima-like assignment and arithmetic subset, including rand(n) for seeded variants and two-integer lcm(a,b). ratsimp preserves a common-denominator form for supported scalar expressions.


Scalar functions
Elementary functions include ln as an alias for log, bounded rational-polynomial gcd(a,b), and real scalar mod(a,b), including Maxima’s mod(x,0)=x. Author expressions also support num, denom, ev(expr), and ev(expr,simp). Symbolic complex logarithms requiring branch proofs remain unsupported.


Tests
AlgEquiv, Sets, SameType, EqualComAss, FacForm, SingleFrac, LowestTerms, NumAbsolute, NumRelative, NumDecPlaces. The four form-sensitive tests require sans to name an input directly. FacForm also requires one polynomial variable in <testoptions> (a symbol or an author alias resolving to one); it checks equivalence and factorization of univariate polynomials over the rationals. Blank or syntactically malformed absolute/relative tolerances default to 0.05, while decimal places require an explicit count from 1 to 50. See the README for the expression whitelist.


PRTs
Acyclic node graphs with =, +, and − score operations, weighted response trees, branch feedback and notes.


Author tests
Native <qtest> inputs and expected PRT score, penalty, and answer note.



This is a deliberately limited evaluator, not a replacement for Moodle STACK or its Maxima CAS. questionsimplify=0 (simp:false) is accepted when any EqualComAss teacher form can be preserved after freezing author variables; otherwise the build rejects it. In this mode, supported {@expression@} CASText also preserves authored arithmetic form and groups substitutions inside existing TeX math. EqualComAss, FacForm, SingleFrac, and LowestTerms require a direct input name in sans to preserve the student’s written form. FacForm considers the written factors, including common integer content, and rejects expressions outside its bounded polynomial subset or a missing/non-symbol variable option. SingleFrac requires an equivalent single written fraction (or equivalent atomic answer) and excludes divisions nested in its numerator or denominator. LowestTerms checks reducible written integer fractions and supported denominator restrictions; it does not compare the teacher expression or factor symbolic polynomials. Build-time validation rejects unsupported author features rather than silently grading them differently. Symbolic equivalence uses SymPy transformations rather than randomized substitution. Decimal-place grading reads the literal answer so a trailing zero is meaningful. Native qtest answer notes are checked using STACK-style ordered subsequence matching, including anchored beginning/end notes and NULL: a terminal note can pass even if earlier PRT nodes contributed notes. The review interface and qtests help an author inspect the selected seeds, but they do not establish complete parity with all STACK configurations.
Finite collections use an algebraic input: square brackets for lists, braces for sets, including nested mixtures and empty collections. Leaves must be scalar expressions. Limits are 32 entries per container, six levels and 128 collection-tree nodes. AlgEquiv recurses by list position and compares normalized set members; Sets explains outer duplicate and missing/extra entries. EqualComAss preserves written arithmetic, list order, and set multiplicity without flattening sets. Written previews display the entered structure. Use direct input names for form tests; held teacher/qtest aliases fail the build if freezing loses their written form.
SameType and checkanswertype=1 follow STACK applicability: wrong-length lists still have the same type, equal-length lists recursively check member types, and any two sets have the same type. They do not replace an equality test or validate every nested set member’s shape. Frozen collection variables must use exact fractions rather than decimal literals.
Decimals anywhere inside a set (including a list within a set) are unsupported; use exact fractions. Direct list answers retain literal scalar decimal comparisons. Collection checks require sans to name the learner input directly: feedback aliases and derived learner collections lose literal precision when serialized. Teacher collections and helper operations must use author values, and transitive decimal aliases are rejected in collection/helper expressions, qtests and CASText.
Decimal list leaves support literal constant arithmetic with integer powers only. Decimal-bearing function calls, symbolic coefficients and transformed collections such as ev([0.1],simp) are rejected; use exact fractions for these expressions. This restriction preserves the decimal spelling and operations needed by native binary64 comparison.
Author-only finite helpers are set, setify, listify, union, intersection, setdifference, member, subsetp and cardinality. They work in simplified question variables, with bounded input/output. listify(set) supports rational scalar members in numeric order; listify(list) keeps the list’s order and repetitions. Freeze helper results before using Sets/EqualComAss; direct helper calls in those held tests, helper feedback variables and questionsimplify=0 helper calls are unsupported. Learners enter collection literals. See the nested and author-helper examples, and the normalization differences.
CASText also renders a scalar equality such as {@p=ta@} as an equation for display. AlgEquiv additionally supports bounded polynomial equation inputs and disjunctions, with root multiplicity retained. For example, a=0 or b=0 matches a*b=0, while a^3*b^3=0 does not. It also supports pure Boolean expressions and elementary hyperbolic functions such as cosh and tanh. See the examples and the README for the precise limits.

title: Authoring and support
text:
Validate and publish
For an extension-only installation, install sympy==1.13.3 in the Python environment used by Quarto. Run python -m stack_sympy.cli test --file questions/polynomial-expansion.xml after placing _extensions/stack-sympy on PYTHONPATH, then render with quarto render. Serve the _site directory through an HTTP server, including locally: python -m http.server --directory _site 8000. Browser grading loads Pyodide and SymPy; its first use downloads runtime packages, so it needs network access. Review the generated question and run its qtests before publishing any assessment. If a source uses features outside the supported subset, #| diagnostics: true displays the location of a build error in the page during authoring; remove it for production so unsupported questions fail the render.
See bounded matrix inputs for fixed and learner-selected dimensions, raw-cell handling and the pinned standalone editor API.

STACK questions with AI Feedback
text:
Bring selected Moodle STACK questions to a teaching website, with SymPy answer checking and AI Feedback for guided hints and explanations. Supported questions run in the learner’s browser without a Moodle session, retaining their XML, response trees and authored question tests.
Quarto turns plain-text teaching material into web pages. This extension adds interactive STACK question cards to those pages, which you can publish as a static website.

title: STACK questions with AI Feedback
STACK questions with AI Feedback
text:
What is supported?
This is a bounded port of STACK, with algebraic inputs, finite nested scalar lists/sets, and numerical inputs and ten answer tests:
AlgEquiv, Sets, SameType, EqualComAss, FacForm, SingleFrac, LowestTerms, NumAbsolute, NumRelative, and NumDecPlaces.
AlgEquiv also handles supported Boolean expressions and polynomial equations. Nested lists and sets support AlgEquiv, Sets, SameType and written-form EqualComAss. Matrices, logical collection members and units inputs, arbitrary Maxima code, and the full Moodle assessment workflow are outside the current scope. See the precise support limits before adapting a question.

Use your own question

Export a supported question from Moodle as STACK XML.
Add STACK SymPy and AI Feedback to a Quarto project, then embed the named question in a page.
Render the project and publish the resulting website.

title: Question corpus
text:
These are 35 native STACK XML questions from the upstream library. Each question below has a local XML download, its pinned upstream source, and a result from the current adapter. The 23 questions whose authored tests passed on every replayed seed have interactive cards. One additional, clearly labeled presentation teaching copy demonstrates a matrix question whose original HTML remains unsupported. Other originals remain available for inspection, with the observed mismatch or unsupported feature shown explicitly.
The reproducible baseline reports 23 passed, 1 with test mismatches, and 11 blocked (3 at import, 8 at instantiation). It retained 82 authored test cases and replayed 162 seed/case combinations across 24 instantiated questions; 2 combinations disagreed. Passing those bounded checks is evidence for the listed seeds, not complete STACK/Maxima parity.
Attribution and reuse. Questions are from STACK / maths/moodle-qtype_stack, pinned at commit 10d323311b7f39fb7b092dd10ce75f7d8632f525. The unchanged question exports carry the CC BY-SA 4.0 license, also included locally; see each pinned source link below. The manifest records the exact upstream path and SHA-256 for every XML file.

text:
Authored test mismatches
These cases disagree with expectations authored in the XML and are kept out of the interactive gallery. Reviewed causes are named below; an authored-test mismatch alone does not identify whether the cause is the port or the original question. The baseline JSON retains the exact expected and observed results.

AlgMap-8.10
Upstream authoring bug in the PRT. At the failing variant, a=8, b=9, c=2, and d=3, so the correct answer is 8*(t+y)/2 + 9*(t+y)/3 = 7*(t+y). Both authored model answers therefore have no fraction operator. The only full-credit branch requires SingleFrac, which rejects this product; every later branch awards zero. Authored tests 1 and 2 nevertheless expect full credit. The pinned native STACK test also rejects 7*(t+y) under SingleFrac. The port’s random choices expose a latent assumption in the original question; this diagnosis uses the fixed values above, rather than assuming Maxima generates those values for the same seed.
Algebra Refresher / 08 Algebraic fractions · 2 failed of 12 replayed seed/case combinations. For seed 1856951054, case 1, input ans = (7*(t + y)): prt1 expected score 1.0 and answer note 1-0-T, but produced score 0.0 and answer note 1-0-F | 1-1-F.
Download original XML · Pinned upstream source · Full replay
